mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5.25% for two consecutive months, long-term discount rates for equities are expected to rise, reducing the present value of future cash flows and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from a baseline of 0% return during similar high-rate periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by at least 0.5% followed by a stabilization signals deflationary expectations, which typically precedes equity risk-on flows and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns within 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < prev_month - 0.5% for one month, then CPIAUCSL stabilizes
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative or flat despite CPIAUCSL meeting the trigger condition (p-value > 0.05 in out-of-sample test).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in employment growth (PAYEMS) of at least 10,000 jobs per month for three consecutive months predicts stronger consumer demand and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > prev_month + 10,000 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive during analogous labor expansion episodes (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) surprises strongly to the upside by at least 2% in two consecutive months, it anticipates business confidence and triggers a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > prev_month * 1.02 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Out-of-sample, 20-day forward returns remain flat or negative during INDPRO positive surprises of similar magnitude (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial supply measured by RSAFS of at least 5% in a month is associated with inventory drawdowns and anticipation of future shortages, which can drive risk-on equity flows and produce positive S&P 500 forward returns within 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during baseline supply expansions (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment (UNRATE) exceeding 5% for two consecutive months indicates a cooling labor market, which often precedes a risk-off environment and is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns remain positive or flat during comparable UNRATE cooling episodes (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising consumer demand proxies (HOUST > prev_month + 1000) accompanied by a decline in inflation (CPIAUCSL < prev_month - 0.3%) jointly predict a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days due to improved demand–price balance.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > prev_month * 1.001 AND CPIAUCSL < prev_month * 0.97 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive during analogous demand–inflation normalization episodes (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a tightening cycle is signaled by FEDFUNDS rising by at least 0.25% in three consecutive months. During this regime, the S&P 500 is expected to underperform over the next 20 trading days due to higher real borrowing costs and reduced risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > prev_month * 1.0025 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns during tightening episodes are not consistently negative (p-value < 0.05 in out-of-sample test).
